title: Arkansas fishing lake on high alert over Bigfoot 'howls'
excerpt: Visitors to a lake in Arkansas have been warned to be on high alert for Bigfoot after a hunter was left terrified by howls.
content:
Visitors to a lake in Arkansas have been warned to be on high alert for Bigfoot after a hunter was left terrified by "howls".

Was Bigfoot heard in Arkansas

Donald Anderson has revealed he was out hunting in the Diamond Bay area of Lake Norfork - a region popular for fishing and outdoor pursuits - on September 28 when he hard blood-curdling screams coming from the trees close to the water.

Reporting the sighting to the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization (BFRO), Donald explained: "[I] heard two howls 15 seconds apart while bowhunting this morning 7:30 am.

"I am 70 years old and have been hunting all my life, I have heard coyotes and wolfs [sic]. This was neither. I have heard the sound before on TV or Youtube on Bigfoot shows that people have recorded.

"I was hunting in the Diamond Bay area on Lake Norfork."

The report prompted BFRO Investigator Matthew Moneymaker to urge other visitors to stay alert as the howls are likely to be heard again in the same area.

He wrote: "There are several large, slow moving, lake-like rivers near the border between Missouri and Arkansas. There are many deer in this region and many Bigfoot reports near these rivers.

"This area next to Lake Norfork (a dammed river) is the type of area where howls like this would occur, or at least be noticed, at this time of year.

"Fortunately, these types of howls carry for a long distance, so if they occur again over next few days in the same area they will be audible from anywhere near Diamond Bay in Lake Norfork."

Matthew went on to urge anyone who hears the howls to get their phone out and attempt to record the sounds.

He added: "It would be great if someone around there could get a recording of these howls. Just record video with your phone to get the sound. Aim it in the direction of the sounds.

"Unlike a road-crossing sighting from a car, the long howls in Fall often last long enough for you to pull out your phone and start recording.

"This particular bow hunter will be more prepared to do that next time.

"When it happens the first time by surprise, the person who hears is listening intently to figure out what is making the sound rather than thinking they should try to record it. It's a different matter on the second occasion.

"These howls were heard yesterday so there's a good chance they will occur again over the next few days or weeks on this side of Lake Norfork."
